summary: Independent Q6 tracing finds a genuinely coupled, stateful solver-visible storage system rather than LOC/module padding. The numeric hard floor is met at 3033 substantive runtime LOC, and the real entrypoint reaches distinct Rust control-plane and C++ durability/MVCC/recovery/operability responsibilities with cross-module invariants and material partial-fix traps; toy-logic and padding risk are LOW.

evidence.observation: Q6 requires independent entrypoint/reachability/module/invariant/state/removal analysis; large_system_strict requires at least 3000 substantive reachable solver-visible runtime/config LOC and no HIGH toy/padding risk.
The task binds the solver environment to /app/stonevault and identifies /app/stonevault as the produced artifact/workdir surface; the difficulty label was not used as Q6 evidence.

The Rust build script compiles and statically links eleven C++ storage units (catalog, codec, common, engine, integrity, lock, maintenance, recovery, snapshot, transactions, WAL), establishing that the native modules are part of the real executable build rather than detached source padding.

The real process entrypoint loads runtime configuration, opens the persistent engine, emits current sequence, parses a continuous operator command stream, enforces session state, dispatches commands, and owns shutdown/error behavior.

BEGIN/PUT/DEL/GET/SCAN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/CHECKPOINT/STATS/HEALTH/QUIT flow through validation and response shaping into an ownership-aware C ABI bridge with explicit status/error/string-lifetime handling.

Engine construction couples durable-path preparation, writer fencing, snapshot store, WAL, recovery, version catalog, transaction IDs and commit sequence; request paths coordinate transaction write sets, WAL ordering/sync, catalog mutation, checkpoints and runtime audits.

Transaction snapshots/write overlays and catalog multi-version histories/conflict checks/audits are distinct state machines whose semantics must agree. Existing starter miswirings (for example snapshot/overlay/conflict helpers not consistently used by engine paths) create cross-module repair traps rather than independent toy functions.

Durability is implemented through framed CRC-bearing WAL records, torn-tail handling, transaction reconstruction, ordered recovered commits, snapshots written through temp-file/fsync/rename, and startup replay. Starter faults such as uncommitted replay promotion, checkpoint-sequence handling and ignored snapshot checksum verification span these layers, demonstrating nontrivial recovery coupling.

STATS reaches runtime audits that cross catalog, active transactions and durable filesystem paths; storage preparation validates writable durable state and operator statistics are derived from live engine state, so the audit/maintenance logic is operationally reachable rather than dead authoring scale.

The task-scoped static complexity report records 3033 substantive runtime LOC (3433 broader native build LOC). Q6 uses this report only for the numeric floor and independently rebuilds the semantic reachability/padding judgment from code.

role_output.SUBSTANTIVE_LOC_ASSESSMENT: 3033 substantive reachable runtime LOC reported for the exact task commit, clearing the >=3000 Q6 floor. Independent code tracing confirms the counted runtime is organized around the actual executable path and live storage/operator workflows rather than generated/vendor/comment/config-volume noise.
MAJOR_MODULES: Rust control plane: config + line I/O + protocol + session + observability + main coordinate process startup, command validation/state and operator responses.
Rust FFI: typed ownership/status/error translation across the C ABI into the native engine.
C++ engine/transactions/catalog: transaction lifecycle, write sets, version histories, visibility/conflict primitives, commit sequencing and request orchestration.
C++ WAL/recovery: record framing/checksums, fsync ordering, torn-tail handling, transaction reconstruction and ordered replay.
C++ snapshot/checkpoint: durable image serialization, temp-file publication, fsync/rename and restart interaction.
C++ lock/maintenance/integrity/codec/common: writer fencing, durable-path setup, live runtime audits/statistics, binary encoding/CRC/syscall helpers and shared storage types.
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Snapshot isolation spans Transaction.snapshot, VersionCatalog visibility/conflict primitives and Engine get/scan/commit; repairing only one caller leaves inconsistent read/conflict behavior.
Read-your-writes and scan semantics span transaction overlays, catalog scans and engine request wiring; the overlay helper cannot be fixed in isolation.

Crash safety spans WAL append/sync, commit ordering, torn-tail replay, snapshot sequence publication, checkpoint WAL lifecycle and recovery sequencing; local fixes can duplicate, lose or resurrect writes.
FFI/protocol correctness spans binary hex validation/encoding, C-string ownership, status codes and Rust response shaping; mismatches can surface as semantic or memory/error-contract failures.
Operator integrity spans catalog audits, transaction audits, filesystem path inspection and engine WAL-size/current-sequence state; STATS/HEALTH consistency depends on multiple components.
role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: Removing roughly 25% (~758 LOC) of the substantive core cannot be done as a responsibility-coherent slice without materially deleting a runtime capability or safety boundary: the Rust protocol/FFI path, transaction+catalog semantics, WAL+recovery, snapshot/checkpoint durability, or live integrity/maintenance surface. The system therefore does not pass the size bar merely through detachable filler.
